Taiwan Oil and Gas Output Rebounds as Workers End Six-Day Strike

TAIPEI – Operations in Taiwan’s oil and gas production sector returned to normal this week following a six-day strike that disrupted output at key facilities. The action, led by the United Petroleum Workers’ Union, began last Tuesday over wage negotiations and safety concerns, halting production at several plants operated by Formex Energy and Eastern Hydrocarbon Resources.

Industry data suggests the work stoppage reduced Taiwan’s daily crude output by 27%, with natural gas deliveries falling by nearly a third, according to the Taiwan Oil & Gas Producers Association. The association’s president, Lee Wen-hua, said on Thursday, “We estimate that around 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day were affected. Immediate impacts were felt across refineries and storage sites, but we are now stabilizing supply.”

The strike concluded late Sunday after government-mediated talks produced a new labor agreement. The settlement includes a 5.5% across-the-board wage increase, enhanced overtime compensation, and a commitment from employers to review safety protocols at extraction and processing facilities.

Union leader Chang Ming-tse described the outcome as “a significant step forward for worker welfare,” adding, “Our members are committed to supporting a safe and productive industry, but we must be heard on essential issues.”

The Ministry of Labor, which facilitated the negotiations, said in a statement, “We are pleased to have achieved a resolution that restores stability to the oil and gas sector while addressing the legitimate concerns of the workforce.”

Analysts estimate the strike will result in a temporary shortfall in domestic inventories, but expect the sector to recover rapidly. “Taiwan’s strategic reserves and rapid restart procedures have minimized the longer-term impact,” said energy analyst Grace Lin of SinoAsia Research. “If agreement terms are implemented as promised, it could set a new standard for labor relations in the industry.”

Formex Energy and Eastern Hydrocarbon Resources both confirmed that production had resumed at all affected sites by Monday afternoon. Output is projected to return to pre-strike levels by the end of the week.
